name: Mémorial des Martyrs de la Déportation

No sculpture: no Modly piece.

name: Église Notre-Dame-de-Lorette

note: Ballu's twin-spired church on the Boulevard Voltaire (1868). Placed on OSM way 63638108's box (osmium, 2026-10-30), −z the portals at bearing 235; the way is replaced. Walls from its ring, the front from one Commons photograph, spires to 68 m (Wikipedia); nave and apse above the walls not checked.

name: Église Saint-Laurent
note: The Gothic church by the Gare de l'Est, its west front of 1866. name: Église Saint-Nicolas-des-Champs

Walls from its ring (the front runs 6.6° off square), front, tower and south flank from a Commons photograph; heights read off it; north side and choir not checked.

note: The long basin of the Jardins du Trocadéro (1937). note: The column of 1808 and its palm-leaf capital on the Place du Châtelet, the gilt Victory, Boizot's four allegories, the four sphinxes (Wikipedia fr). Elevation from three Commons photographs.

The figure, the gilt flame and the tablet's two dates from a Commons photograph; the pedestal by eye, no source for its height found.

name: CNIT
note: The vault of 1958 (Camelot, de Mailly, Zehrfuss; Prouvé; reglazed 2009): triangle of 218 m a side on three abutments (OSM relation 3071527 and parts, all replaced), 46.3 m at the crown (Wikipedia fr, matching the 46 m BD TOPO apex). Three corrugated shell lobes meeting in valleys to the corners, white rim, inclined glass arches with vertical fins, Hilton/office blocks inside. Shape from Commons photos: Puteaux - Centre des nouvelles industries et technologies - 2025-10-08 17-14-11 001.jpg and 2010-09-28 - CNIT Paris 22.jpg.

name: Tour First
note: KPF 2011 rebuild of Tour UAP: Y plan of three wings (NW 231 m, E 190 m, S 170 m, each with a 25 m sloped glass screen), core crown and mast to 259 m, 16 m glass atrium base. Plan and part heights from OSM parts (osmium, local pbf); look from Commons 'Tour First - La Defense - Inauguration 6 mai 2011.jpg'. Lidar not measured.

name: Les 4 Temps
note: Westfield Les 4 Temps: OSM way 396802664's outline (defense-famous/quatreTemps.ts). Glazed shopfronts on the parvis faces, glass entrance with the red Westfield band and sloped glass canopy at the top of the steps (OSM flights, 48.89142,2.2365), roof car-park decks at the east end. Generic OSM buildings inside the footprint claimed (osmium, 2026-11-16). Roof height by eye over the parvis.

name: Dôme Imax
note: The glass ball by the Grande Arche: OSM part way 186981683, named, 38 m across and height 27. Its grid of panes from the same Commons photograph as Le Dôme's.

name: L'Araignée Rouge
note: Calder's Grand Stabile Rouge: OSM way 186981704 (height 15), which is replaced. Its silhouette traced from one Commons photograph; the cross plates from memory. Which side of it faces bearing 206 was not checked against the outline.

name: Le Pouce
note: César's bronze thumb, height 12 and 4.4 × 4.5 m from OSM way 186981693, which is replaced. No usable photograph was fetched: the shape is simply a thumb's, and the bearing, nail side toward 206, is a guess.

name: Fers
note: Driss Sans-Arcidet's monument to General Dumas (2009), OSM node 7952476083. Shape and sizes by eye from Commons 'Unchained (64188317).jpeg': tall ring with broken chain, cuff with hanging chain; bearing a guess.

name: Monument des Droits de l'Homme
note: Jantzen and Theimer's mastaba-like tower of 1989 in the Champ de Mars (Wikidata Q3323344). Placed on the centre of OSM way 369434380 (a 14.5 m square podium turned 45 deg; osmium, 2026-11-22), the front (−z) the south-west face toward the Champ de Mars at bearing 225, the bronze door on the back. Podium from OSM; the tower (~7.2 m wide, 12 m tall), the two bronze obelisks (~14.5 m) and the figures' places are scaled off one wide photograph against the figures, not surveyed; the seals, triangle and sundial are stand-ins. The figures are Modly models (statues manifest: droits-group, droits-toga).

name: Fontaine aux roseaux d'argent
note: Brigitte Nahon's c. 2000 fountain (Wikidata Q18146923) in the rose garden of the Jardin médiéval du musée de Cluny (public, outdoors): a narrow timber-edged channel ~12 m long ending in a clump of twisting stainless-steel reeds with glass beads, two glass light wells and a plaque at the near end. The Wikidata point is rounded (48.851, 2.344); placed on the wooden-edged band an IGN ortho shows in the garden's east bed, running WNW-ESE, the reeds at the WNW end (front = 287): the channel's exact spot and which end the reeds are on are guessed. Dimensions scaled off two Commons photos against the planks (+-30 %). The thin steel blades are procedural ribbons (too thin for Modly); no OSM way is mapped for it.

name: Fontaine Louvois
note: Visconti's cast-iron fountain of 1844 in the square Louvois (Wikidata Q3076038; sculptor Klagmann): octagonal basin (OSM way 26277959, ~6 m flat to centre, a sloppy polygon so +-1 m; vertices near east, hence front 25), square pedestal with four tritons on dolphins, a wide bowl with zodiac band and mascarons, an upper pedestal, the four river goddesses back to back under the top bowl. Basin from OSM; bowls, pedestals and the ~8.5 m total height scaled off Commons photographs against the 3.6 m goddess group, not surveyed. Goddesses and top bowl are a Modly model (statues manifest: louvois-group), the tritons likewise (louvois-triton).

name: Fontaine Baqué (rue Prudent-Jassedé, Issy)
note: Pierre Baqué's 1992 fountain (stainless steel and masonry) in the stepped pedestrian rue Prudent-Jassedé, Issy-les-Moulineaux; OSM node 4962502455 'Fontaine'. Round brick-lipped basin with leaning steel spikes, three tall banded-drum columns (two carrying a lintel), four stumps. Only two Commons photos (from above): sizes and the layout's orientation are guessed; no Modly pieces (the steel spikes are procedural).

name: Fontaine des Polypores (rue Modigliani)
note: Jean-Yves Lechevallier's 1982 fountain (Wikidata Q23459533, OSM way 291115567) at the rue Saint-Charles end of the rue Modigliani, 15e: a round basin with wide coping and two heaps of tilted stone dishes ('the bracket fungi'). Placed on the centroid of the OSM basin way (~5 m radius plus coping); the dishes' number, sizes and the 3.4 m and 2.6 m heights are scaled off two Commons photographs, not surveyed. Procedural dishes (seeded tilted lathe bowls), no Modly piece.

name: Fontaine de la Paix (Détournelle)
note: Détournelle's stone pylon fountain of 1806-10 in the allée du Séminaire off the rue Bonaparte (Wikidata Q3076202, monument historique 1926, reliefs by Voinier, Espercieux, Caraffe, Marquois): a plinth, a die with garland frieze and a pediment on each long face, four relief panels (A LA PAIX, SCIENCES ET ARTS, AGRICULTURE, COMMERCE), a mascaron and shell bowl on each long face, in a rectangular trough. Trough 5.3 x 3.8 m from OSM way 1200013023 (centre taken from it); the pylon's ~1.8 x 1.2 m die and ~5.2 m height scaled off Commons photographs against the trough, not surveyed. Reliefs are drawn as shallow dark panels (procedural, no Modly pieces). Which long face is the front (bearing) is a guess from the photos.

name: La Danse de la fontaine émergente
note: Chen Zhen's 2008 dragon-fountain on the place Augusta-Holmès (Wikidata Q747835; OSM node 447873149 is a point, no footprint to claim): a row of glass tubes with water inside breaking the paving, ringed with steel hoops and crested with scalloped steel fins. Procedural only (monument-kit sweptTube/hoop/finPlate). Hump count (5), length (~30 m), height (~2.1 m) and the serpentine are read off ONE Commons photo (Place_Augusta_Holmes_03) against a car and lamp post, not surveyed; orientation (front 0) is a guess: check against an aerial. The head is not visible in the photo, so the body just dives under at both ends. No Modly part: nothing figurative survives.

name: Fontaine Molière
note: Visconti's wall fountain of 1844 at the corner of rue de Richelieu and rue Molière (Wikidata Q3076047; Seurre's bronze Molière, Pradier's two Muses): a shell-headed niche between pairs of Corinthian columns, entablature dated MDCCCXLIV, an arched pediment, the dedication pedestal, a stepped basin. Claims OSM way 54097804 (the fountain mapped as a building, ~8.3 m across the back, back wall on its SW edge, front toward the place Mireille at bearing 39). Heights (~12 m) and the 2.4 m seated bronze scaled off Commons photographs, not surveyed; the tympanum relief is a stand-in. Molière and the Muses are Modly models (statues manifest: moliere-seated, moliere-muse-1, moliere-muse-2).

name: Fontaine Gaillon
note: Visconti's wall fountain of 1828 on the south face of the corner house in the place Gaillon (Wikidata Q579833): shell-headed niche between two Corinthian columns, entablature, attic with the MDCCCXXVII dedication and two urns, two-tier basin on balusters, a putto on a dolphin on the upper bowl (Modly, gaillon-dauphin). The host house (OSM way 54531802, apartments) is NOT claimed; the model starts at its south face (y 949.3 in the paris-centre frame), centred on its middle (x 169.1). Dimensions are scaled off two Commons photos against column spacing ~4 m, not surveyed; lower rim ~1.5 m is the shakiest figure.

name: Fontaine Pastorale
note: Desruelles' high relief of 1923 (shepherd, sheep, girl) in Chauvigny stone on a wall fountain built 1925 by the architect Ollivier, against the south face of the church Saint-Germain-des-Prés' chapel wall in the square Félix-Desruelles (Wikidata Q3076051; the Wikidata point lies 4 m south of the wall). Placed on the south edge of OSM wall way 1461285705 / building strip way 1461285706 (osmium), front bearing 192.6 off that edge; the church wall is the church model's and OSM's, not claimed. Base, three rosette spouts, trough, water and slab are procedural, scaled off two Commons photographs against the figures taken as ~1.4 m tall (not surveyed; the slab height is a guess); the relief group is a Modly model (statues manifest pastorale-group).

name: Fontaine Sainte-Geneviève
note: Wall fountain of 1864 (Wikidata Q3076089) in the place Jacqueline-de-Romilly, rue Descartes / rue de la Montagne-Sainte-Geneviève, opposite the old École polytechnique: a semicircular stone wall ~6 m across (fr.wikipedia) with a blue iron railing, a pier with the city's shield at each end, a chain across the open side and three blue lion-head mascarons pouring into floor gratings (the lion is a Modly model, sainte-genevieve-lion). Plan from OSM's untagged 12-point arc at the corner (radius ~3 m, chord tilted ~12 deg; no building way to claim); wall height, pier height and railing taken off one Commons photograph against the lion head, not surveyed.

name: Fontaine de la Reine
note: The dry 16th-c. wall fountain (Beausire 1732; Wikidata Q15948824, MH 1994) in the rounded south-west corner of the Aubry house, rue Saint-Denis 142 at rue Greneta: plinth with table panel, round-headed niche (spout and mascaron lost), cornice on two bearded mascaron corbels, royal cartouche, upper window. Placed on the OSM house corner (way 1101931, not claimed; model origin = its SW corner vertex, 10 m from Wikidata's point). Heights by eye off Commons photos against the street plaques (~0.3 m wide), good to ~0.3 m; the niche back stands 0.62 m in front of the house corner so shop boards clear.

name: Fontaine de Paradis
note: Dry wall fountain (Guillain 1636, Beausire 1705; Wikidata Q3076159) in the rounded SW corner pavilion of the Hôtel de Soubise, rue des Francs-Bourgeois at rue des Archives: scallop-headed niche, sill ledge, plain panel below, dedication plaque above. Placed on the chamfer of OSM way 6742329 (Soubise, NOT claimed; niche back 0.55 m in front of its face). Sizes scaled off Commons photos against the poster door (~2.6 m), the sill height is a guess; the real wall is curved, the model is flat. No sculpture, so no Modly piece.

name: Puits artésien de la Butte-aux-Cailles
note: Drinking fountain of the artesian well (Q16671566, place Paul-Verlaine, 13e): grey stone trough under an arched polished-steel pipe on a post, steel guard rail, drain grating. Placed on OSM's drinking_water node (2.3527043, 48.827691), not Wikidata's rounder point; no building way under it, so nothing to claim. Sizes scaled by eye off the one Commons photo (Artesienbutteauxcaillesparis.jpg), trough ~1.5 m long and the pipe ~1.5 m high are guesses; the info panel and wall behind are not modelled; the facing (rotateDeg) is a guess. No sculpture, so no Modly piece.

name: Fontaine du Coq
note: Fontaine du Coq (Wikidata Q41621277; frwiki): free-standing stone aedicule at the dead end of the avenue du Coq (9e), last remnant of the château des Porcherons: two piers, shell-headed niche, shell frieze, fish-and-trident relief over the keystone, half-round basin; the cast-iron fountain in the niche is Modly (coq-fontaine). Placed at the south end of OSM way 93530778 (Wikidata's point and the list's row sit on it); no OSM building under it, nothing claimed. Sizes scaled off one Commons photo assuming a 3.8 m width: not surveyed.

name: Fontaine du Vert Bois
note: The 1712 wall fountain of the rue Saint-Martin / rue du Vertbois (Wikidata Q3076291): a stone portal against the foot of the Saint-Martin-des-Champs tower, rusticated pilasters, relief, bronze plaque, shell and bronze mascaron spout, cornice and a cartouche of arms on top (Modly: vertbois-crown, vertbois-mascaron). OSM way 54964126 (amenity=fountain) claimed. Faces the rue Saint-Martin / rue du Vertbois junction (front 335, NNW), the tower to its right: read off OSM's footway/fence line and the junction position, not checked on site. Dimensions scaled off Commons photos at ~80 px/m (pilaster ~0.9 m), not surveyed; heights shakiest.

name: Regard de la fontaine du Pré-Saint-Gervais
note: The stone regard (inspection house) of the old Pré-Saint-Gervais aqueduct with a public fountain in its front, place Anatole-France / rue André-Joineau, Le Pré-Saint-Gervais (Wikidata Q3076279; monument historique inscrit 1899, PA00079946). Footprint and facing from OSM way 73248961 (building, claimed): 3.3 m across the front, 4.3 m deep, the front (-z) toward the west street (front 275.8); the apartment block 5 m behind it on the east side matches the Commons photograph. Heights (5.0 m eaves, porch cornice 2.5 m, 5.7 m roof top) read off the photograph against bollards, not surveyed. No sculpture: the pine-cone finial is a lathe.

name: Fontaine Childebert
note: The Childebert (abbaye Saint-Germain) wall fountain of 1715-17 re-erected in the square Paul-Langevin (Wikidata Q3076004): ashlar pier with pilasters, shell niche, sunk panel, shelf, bronze mascaron (Modly) and a low curved basin, against the trellised terrace wall. Position: the Commons geotag (48.84768, 2.35025) moved ~3.5 m SW to the foot of the terrace wall seen in the game; front and dimensions estimated from photos (not surveyed). No OSM way mapped for it.

name: Fontaine Dejean
note: Formigé's fountain of 1906 (Q3076013, OSM node 2482248710) in the square de la place Pasdeloup beside the Cirque d'Hiver: octagonal base with carved frieze, two scallop shells, gadrooned bowl, tapering shaft with Dejean's oval portrait medallion and inscription, acanthus vase and sphere under a pelican (Modly, dejean-pelican). No OSM way to claim (a node). Heights and widths are scaled off Commons photos against the medallion (~0.4 m) and base (~1 m across), not surveyed; the facing (medallion to the south) is a guess.

name: Fontaine de Jarente
note: The 1783 stone pavilion closing the impasse de la Poissonnerie off the rue de Jarente (Wikidata Q1435786), 4.7 m wide like OSM's end wall (the host houses are OSM ways 56045039 / 1174634452, not claimed; the model stands 0.6 m in front of their face). Rusticated pilasters, entablature, pediment with a shell cartouche, stepped pyramid roof, cartouche panel, plain tablet, mask spout and trough, all procedural (the cartouche is shallow relief: no Modly piece). Dimensions scaled off Commons photographs against the side doors and the OSM wall width, not surveyed; roof heights are guessed; front bearing 207 read from the end wall's normal.

name: Fontaine du Marché-aux-Carmes
note: Fragonard's herm fountain of 1830, moved to the square Gabriel-Pierné (rue de Seine / rue Mazarine, 6e) in 1930 (Wikidata Q3076266; the old Marché des Carmes was at place Maubert, but the fountain stands here, at the list's coordinates). Basin radius 1.32 m from OSM way 1200620877 (claimed); pillar 0.64 x 0.46 m, 2.5 m to the shoulders, spouts at 1.0 m, scaled off three Commons photos against the basin width, not surveyed. The two-faced head with its fruit-basket crown is a Modly model (carmes-head), made from one face's photos so only one face is real; the bust fronts on the pillar are flat stand-ins.

name: Fontaine du Château d'eau de Montmartre
note: Titeux's wall fountain of 1835 on the front of the old Montmartre reservoir (9b rue Norvins, Wikidata Q945052; OSM way 77937860, the disused reservoir building, claimed: ring extruded as the body, front on its SSW edge, bearing 197). Aedicule 5 m wide, ~7.2 m to the pediment, 8-step stair, niche 2.6 m wide, scaled off two Commons photos against the niche and stair, not surveyed; pink marble panels and the frieze are flat stand-ins. The bronze vase with dolphin feet in the niche is a Modly model (reservoir-vase).

name: Fontaine aux Lions de Nubie
note: Girard's fountain of 1811 (fontaine du Château d'eau, Q3076267) in the Place de la Fontaine-aux-Lions, La Villette; OSM way 81752247 (a 0.6 m wall outline, ~26 m across, claimed). Pool, two round steps, four diagonal piers, core and two-tazza plume are by eye from Commons photographs (Fontaine Château Eau Pierre Simon Girard Paris 1-4): radii and heights are guesses, only the 26 m outline is measured. The eight cast-iron lions (two a pier) are Modly pieces attached from paris-statues.json at LION_AT.

name: Fontaine du puits de Grenelle
note: The fountain of 1906 (Q3076301) in the round planter of place Georges-Mulot, 15e, on the site of the first artesian well; OSM way 252282895 (natural=water, the 3.4 m planter circle) claimed. Square ashlar shaft with four engaged corner columns, plinth, oval medallions on the four faces, cornice, stepped stone cap and ball. Heights and widths are scaled off the Commons photo 'Fontaine du Puits de Grenelle.jpg' against the mascaron (~0.33 m) and plinth (~2.1 m), not surveyed; medallions/frames are shallow relief kept procedural. The bronze mascaron (south face) is a procedural stand-in: three Modly attempts (hunyuan21, trellis2 x2) from the only usable photo (~140 px of face) gave flat slabs, so none is published.

name: Monument à Gavarni
note: Denys Puech and Henri Guillaume's monument of 1904 (Q3076026, OSM node tagged amenity=fountain) in the middle of the place Saint-Georges roundabout: iron railing, round basin, square plinth with a bronze mask on two sides, a stout round column carrying Gavarni's carnival figures in high relief, frieze, cornice and the half-length statue of Gavarni. Dimensions scaled by eye off Commons photos (Monument Gavarni 2021-06-27 -3/-5, Fontaine Gavarni Paris 9e) against the railing (~1 m); about 7.4 m in all, not surveyed. Which way the front faces is a guess (-z). No OSM building ways under it.

name: Fontaine du Bassin Soufflot
note: Davioud's basin (1862) in the place Edmond-Rostand, 6e, with Crauk's bronze Triton and nereid holding a shell (Q3076290; OSM way 685770760, fountain+water+wall height 0.5, ring radius ~7 m measured). Rim width, the 8 support blocks and the ring of small jets are by eye off Commons photos; the group is Modly soufflot-triton.

name: Fontaine de la Porte Dorée
note: Cascade fountain of 1931 (Q3076201, place Édouard-Renard) with Drivier's gilded Athena on a granite column at its high end. Axis, 7 steps of 8.2 m, the 4 m channel and the column's node from OSM way 130888780 (osmium, 2026-11-23); the ground climbs 2.2 m foot to column (terrain). Cheek widths, the 8 m top pool, column 1.7 x 3.4 m and the gilt base are by eye off Commons photos, not surveyed. The Athena is Modly (statues manifest porte-doree-athena).

name: Fontaine de l'Avril
note: Pierre Roche's Art nouveau fountain of 1906 in the square Brignole-Galliera beside the Palais Galliera, 16e (Q3076179; OSM way 262367200, fountain+water, ring radius ~4.5 m measured, centred on the ring, ~3 m from the Wikidata point). Procedural: low round basin, two stone drums, tapering verdigris pylon with a leafy collar. Heights, pylon width and rim are by eye off Commons photos (Fontaine d'Avril - Galliera, Statue 01) against the Palais Galliera plinth, not surveyed. The bronze girl with the flower hat is Modly avril-fillette.

name: Fontaine de la place François-Ier
note: Davioud's fountain with Murguet's sculpture (1865), made for the place de la Madeleine and moved here about 1909 (Q3076214; its twin is in the place Santiago-du-Chili; frwiki). Centred on the OSM basin way 553172931 (water=basin, ring radius ~2.8 m measured). Procedural: round basin, lobed foot and four plinth blocks, gadrooned drum, the vasque with lion-head spouts, openwork gallery and falls, a plain shaft. Heights and the vasque width are scaled off Commons photos (vue globale, socle, haut) against the basin ring, not surveyed. Modly: francois-ier-griffon (four winged griffins) and francois-ier-fut (shaft with four paired masks and the flared openwork cup).

name: Fontaine des Ambassadeurs
note: Hittorff's fountain of 1840 in the jardins des Champs-Elysees (Q3076221; OSM way 67091995, amenity=fountain + water, 5.6 m across, measured): low round stone basin, square panelled pedestal, reed-and-mask cluster, wide cast-iron bowl with eight mascarons spilling into the basin, bronze nymph on top (Modly ambassadeurs-nymphe). Every height and the bowl and pedestal widths are by eye off Commons photos (Fontaine des Ambassadeurs Paris 8e 001/003) against the basin wall, not surveyed.

name: Fontaine de la Petite-Halle
note: Beausire's free-standing ashlar fountain pavilion of 1719 at the rue du Faubourg-Saint-Antoine / rue de Montreuil (Q3076204, also Fontaine de Montreuil; OSM way 63649496, claimed, 4.5 x 5.2 m with its niche dent). Stepped plinth, corner pilasters, cornice, pediment on each face, hipped roof; arched niche with trough and the bearded bronze mascaron (Modly montreuil-mascaron); blind arches/oculi on the sides, a door at the back. Heights, which face is which and the door side read off two Commons photos against the door (~2 m), not surveyed.

name: Miroir d'eau, la Seine et ses affluents
note: Raoul Larche's fountain of 1900-1901 in the square Jean-Perrin beside the Grand Palais (Q3076034): a lobed oval marble basin with the Seine and her tributaries seated on its rim. Plan = OSM ways 66758129 (outer) and 66758138 (water), measured; rim height 0.6 m and group sizes by eye against Commons photos. The sculpture groups are Modly pieces in paris-statues.json.

name: Bassin rond du Petit Palais (sud)
note: One of the four small round basins of the 1900 layout round the Grand and Petit Palais (Q2887588; south-east round basin at the foot of the avenue Winston-Churchill, Petit Palais side; Wikidata Q2887588 'bassins du Petit et Grand Palais' = six basins; OSM way 66768636, ~8 m across, rim 0.2 tagged). Rim width, the cast-iron reed cluster and the tall jet are by eye off Commons (Fontaine du Grand Palais, Fontaine du Petit Palais); no Modly (the reeds are a 0.6 m ornament, procedural).

name: Bassin rond du Grand Palais (sud)
note: One of the four small round basins of the 1900 layout round the Grand and Petit Palais (Q2887588; south-west round basin, Grand Palais side; Wikidata Q2887588 'bassins du Petit et Grand Palais' = six basins; OSM way 66755254, ~8 m across, rim 0.2 tagged). Rim width, the cast-iron reed cluster and the tall jet are by eye off Commons (Fontaine du Grand Palais, Fontaine du Petit Palais); no Modly (the reeds are a 0.6 m ornament, procedural).

name: Bassin rond du Grand Palais (nord)
note: One of the four small round basins of the 1900 layout round the Grand and Petit Palais (north-west round basin, Grand Palais side; Wikidata Q2887588 'bassins du Petit et Grand Palais' = six basins; OSM way 66755262, ~8 m across, rim 0.2 tagged). Rim width, the cast-iron reed cluster and the tall jet are by eye off Commons (Fontaine du Grand Palais, Fontaine du Petit Palais); no Modly (the reeds are a 0.6 m ornament, procedural).

name: Bassin rond du Petit Palais (nord)
note: One of the four small round basins of the 1900 layout round the Grand and Petit Palais (north-east round basin, Petit Palais side; Wikidata Q2887588 'bassins du Petit et Grand Palais' = six basins; OSM way 66768651, ~8 m across, rim 0.2 tagged). Rim width, the cast-iron reed cluster and the tall jet are by eye off Commons (Fontaine du Grand Palais, Fontaine du Petit Palais); no Modly (the reeds are a 0.6 m ornament, procedural).

name: Bassin ovale du Petit Palais (Champs-Élysées)
note: The oval basin on the Champs-Élysées promenade east of the avenue Winston-Churchill (OSM way 66768655, 11.7 x 8 m measured; its west twin is the next entry; Larche's Miroir d'eau is a separate basin). Vase bowl, jet and the small bronze dolphins are procedural stand-ins by eye off Commons (Bassin du Grand Palais 5): Modly not attempted.

name: Bassin ovale du Grand Palais (square de Berlin)
note: The oval basin on the Champs-Élysées promenade west of the avenue Winston-Churchill, Grand Palais side (OSM way 66768634, 11.5 x 7.8 m measured, rim 0.5 tagged; not the Miroir d'eau, which is Larche's separate basin in square Jean-Perrin). Vase bowl, jet and small bronze dolphins are procedural stand-ins by eye off Commons (Bassin du Grand Palais 5): Modly not attempted.

name: L'Embâcle (Daudelin, place du Québec)
note: Charles Daudelin's 1984 fountain-sculpture in the place du Québec (Q3076308): bronze plates tilted up out of the paving round a shallow pool. All procedural (src/render/landmarks/paris/monuments/minor/fontaine-embacle.ts, kit tiltedSlab). Position and pool footprint from OSM way 664223075 (the Wikidata/list coordinate 48.85330,2.33306 is ~28 m south, inside an apartment block, so it was not used). Plate count, tilts, sizes and the ~1.6 m peak are by eye off two Commons photos, not surveyed.

name: Fontaine de Joyeuse
note: Boitel's stone edicule of 1847 at 41 rue de Turenne (Q3076142, also Fontaine Saint-Louis): fluted pilasters on pedestals, entablature with the arms of Paris, archivolt over a semi-domed niche, iron grille, lobed tazza over a half-round basin, the zinc child with a jar (Modly joyeuse-enfant). Real one is recessed into the house; here it stands about 1 m proud, its back 0.55 m in front of the house face (OSM building ways at x about 2369.7 not claimed; the face line and its 92 degree normal read off the OSM polygon, so the model centre is 1 m east of it). Width ~3.3 m from frwiki (about 3 m) and photos; heights scaled against a scooter, not surveyed.

name: Monument aux soldats noirs morts pour la France
note: Stele in the Jardin d'agronomie tropicale (Q17745972, OSM memorial node, memorial=stele; Wikidata gives 48.8332 2.4661): a pale stone slab with a bas-relief of a woman beside a Poilu's helmet, on an inscribed die, three steps and a low wing wall each side. Placed on the OSM node; facing south (away from the Pavillon de l'Indochine, per the 1900s postcard) is a guess. Dimensions by eye off Commons photographs (die ~2 m wide), not surveyed. The woman is Modly soldatsnoirs-femme (paris-statues.json).

name: Monument aux morts parisiens de la Première Guerre mondiale
note: Q95124483, 2018 (Phileas architecture): a 280 m long, 1.30 m high wall of dark blue steel plates carrying the 94,415 names, along the boulevard de Ménilmontant face of the Père-Lachaise wall (OSM way 13859706 runs (4181,-34)-(4099,221) in game metres, 283 m, which matches). Placed along that wall 0.9 m street-side of the OSM line, front facing WSW toward the boulevard (Wikidata's point sits on the wall, 33 m from the carriageway). Length and height are written figures; plate pitch, lettering and plinth guessed; the wall climbs 3.9 m north (baked ground at the wall, tools/at-point.ts) so the builder steps each plate up by the RISE table. No sculpture, so no Modly piece.

name: Monument aux Volontaires américains
note: Jean Boucher's monument of 1923 to the American volunteers of 1914-17 (Q19945167) in the square Thomas-Jefferson, on OSM building way 79657347 (3.5 x 5.7 m, long side N-S; claimed so it is not drawn as a generic block). Procedural: two steps, a figure ledge, a pale limestone block with plinth course, cornice, carved wing rows and an attic plinth. Front facing west (toward the square's long axis and the steps' side) is a guess, turned to 270 after a first shot showed the east face is the plain back. Heights scaled by eye off Commons photos, not surveyed. Modly: volontaires-groupe (the relief group, French and American soldiers clasping hands before a winged Victory) and volontaires-soldat (the bronze soldier with raised arm).

name: Monument à Komitas
note: Bronze Komitas by David Erevantsi (2003, Q3323366) on a plain limestone cube at the west end of the Cours Albert-1er, placed on Wikidata's coordinates (no OSM building there). Pedestal ~1.6 x 1.4 x 1.5 m and statue ~2.8 m estimated off Commons photos, not surveyed; the inscription face toward the south is a guess. The statue is Modly komitas-statue (paris-statues.json).

name: Tombe du Dragon (Père-Lachaise)
note: Stele of Antoine de Guillaume-Lagrange, dragoon (Q3531119, 1809): round-topped limestone stele on a step base, shallow relief of the helmeted bust in a laurel wreath, sabre, musket, mourning figure and inscription; back all inscription. No sculpture in the round, so no Modly piece. Placed on Wikidata's coordinates (no OSM way there). Sizes (~0.62 m wide, 1.7 m tall) estimated off Commons photos against the base, not surveyed; facing south is a guess.

name: Mémorial du vol Air France 447 (Père-Lachaise)
note: Memorial to the 228 dead of AF447 (2009), division 84, Q96106655, on Wikidata's coordinates (no OSM way of its own). Procedural only, no sculpture: black granite slab with names face, upright engraved glass pane behind, four paving slabs in front; sizes estimated off one Commons photo (Division 84 - AF 447 memorial 02), facing unverified.

name: Monument aux soldats tchécoslovaques (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q96035892 (unveiled 19 Dec 1934), division 84 on the avenue des Combattants étrangers, on Wikidata's point. Form read off Commons photos (panoramio 'Monument Honoring Czech Volunteers', Flickr 31328958391): a wide pink-grey granite slab in three joined panels with the Czech and French dedications, a bronze group on top (Modly piece monument-soldats-tchecoslovaques-groupe) and a small WWII plaque on the paving. No OSM building under it. Slab width ~3.7 m, height ~1.2 m, group ~1.9 m are estimated against the figures; rotateDeg 0 is a guess (front faces -z) pending a look at the avenue.

name: Stèle du génocide des Tutsi au Rwanda (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q96080492 (its Wikidata label is the Abdellys stele but the point and Commons 'Père-Lachaise - Division 88 - Rwanda genocide memorial 01-06' show this one). Pale limestone stele on a low plinth: arched-top panel between two capped shoulders, tan engraved plaque 'En 1994 au Rwanda plusieurs centaines de milliers de Tutsi ont été victimes d'un génocide'. All procedural, no sculpture, no Modly. Sizes (~1.6 m wide, ~1.1 m high) estimated against the hedge and flowers; rotateDeg a guess pending a look at the path. No OSM building way under it.

name: Monument aux victimes de l'Opéra-Comique
note: Q15156006 (1888), common grave of the 25 May 1887 Opéra-Comique fire in Père-Lachaise division 96, on Wikidata's point. Form read off two Commons photos (Division 96 - Opéra-Comique 01, 03): two broad grey stone steps with a thick round-shouldered inscribed stele; no sculpture, so no Modly piece. Dimensions (steps ~2.9 x 2.7 m, stele ~1.35 m) and the facing direction are estimated by eye, not surveyed.

name: Monument aux morts pour la France en Afrique du Nord (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q96091551, division 88, allée des Fédérés, on Wikidata's point (the OSM node is a plaque, no building way). Form read off Commons Division 88 01-03: paved court with two entry steps, two-tier back wall (plain lower wall, name-panel band above on a shadow gap), inclined side wings, tall inscribed grey stele on a low ledger; no sculpture, so no Modly piece. All dimensions (court ~7.4 x 4.6 m, stele ~2.3 m, wall ~6.4 m wide) and the facing direction are estimated by eye, not surveyed.

name: Fontaine du jardin Villemin
note: Cast-iron fountain by Marie-Auguste Martin (Val d'Osne, 1846; Q3076294; MH 1970), moved to the jardin Villemin (canal Saint-Martin side) in the 1970s; still there (Commons photos 2010s). Placed on OSM's fountain node n1700445942 (Wikidata's point is 2 m off); no OSM building under it. Plinth and footing procedural, about 1.05 x 0.85 x 0.62 m, estimated off Commons photos against a lamp post (about 2.0 m in all); the tritons, bowl and child are one Modly piece (villemin-fontaine). Rotation guessed.

name: Monument à Octave Gréard
note: Fontaine Octave Gréard (Q2372689; Nénot architect, Chaplain sculptor, 1909), square Samuel-Paty, on the east edge of the square beside the place Paul-Painlevé; placed on OSM's artwork node n9426205207 (Wikidata's point is 6 m off), front (the relief face) toward the garden, i.e. west-north-west. No OSM building under it. A stone arch on a low base, battered piers, urns, a cartouche, the bust in the opening, a low relief of a schoolmistress and a child below: sizes (~5 m wide, ~4.9 m to the crown, base 1 m) scaled off Commons photographs against the bust, not surveyed. The relief stays procedural (shallow); the bust is Modly greard-buste (paris-statues.json). The two threads of water frwiki mentions are not visible in the photographs, so none is drawn.

name: Mémorial national de la guerre d'Algérie (quai Branly)
note: Q3333171, 2002 (Gérard Collin-Thiébaut): three pale columns 5.85 m high (Wikipedia) with scrolling-name displays in blue, white and red on both broad faces. Placed on the centre of OSM way 814263041 (18.3 x 10.7 m, long axis NE-SW along the quai). Column width 0.85, depth 0.42, spacing 2.7 m and the display strip are estimated off a Commons photo; the displays are static lit dashes.

name: Monument du corps expéditionnaire russe
note: Monument à la mémoire du corps expéditionnaire russe (Q18168657), place du Canada / cours la Reine: Sourovtsev's 2011 bronze soldier with his grazing horse on a low black granite plinth with a French bronze plaque and a Russian lettered cap band. Placed on Wikidata's point (no OSM building there). Plinth ~3.0 x 1.24 x 1.0 m and the 1.9 m group estimated off Commons photographs (Monument Corps expéditionnaire russe Paris 1-3), not surveyed; which long face is the plaque face (here south) is a guess. The group is Modly russe-soldat-cheval (paris-statues.json).

name: Fontaine du square Lamartine
note: Fontaine à l'Albien / puits artésien de Passy (Q3076297), square Lamartine: the 1950s travertine block (Dupuis) over the 1861 well, a grey plaque on the broad face and a tap on the narrow one. Placed on frwiki's coordinates (OSM has only the tap node, 48.86525 2.27549, no building). Block ~3.2 x 2.0 x 2.6 m estimated off one Commons photo (Puits artésien sq Lamartine.jpg), not surveyed; plan orientation (rotateDeg) is a guess. No sculpture, so no Modly pieces.

name: Monument aux morts du Père-Lachaise
note: Bartholome's war memorial (1899, Q3323309; OSM way 311412497, width 14.1, height 8): a limestone mausoleum front at the top of the Avenue Principale steps, doorway with the couple (Modly pere-couple), a mourning group each side (pere-gauche, pere-droite), the sunk panel of the dead (shallow, procedural), bronze wing doors with step flights. Placed at the OSM polygon's long front edge (osmium; facing bearing 241.9, down the steps). Dimensions scaled by eye off Commons photographs against the 14.1 m OSM width, not surveyed.

name: Fontaine du Cirque
note: Hittorff and Barre's cast-iron fountain of 1839 in the jardins des Champs-Elysees (Wikidata Q3076259, OSM way 67036988 whose water ring is only ~3 m radius): wide low round stone basin (~8.3 m across by eye off Commons photos, a bench and people as scale), octagonal pedestal, big bowl with twelve lion mascarons, the four Seasons (children) back to back under a smaller bowl with dog and wolf heads. Sizes are estimates, not surveyed. The children group is a Modly model (statues manifest: cirque-saisons).

name: Fontaine de Diane
note: Hittorff's fountain of 1840 (Q3076128; also fontaine Ledoyen) in the jardin des Champs-Élysées, sister of the Cirque, Ambassadeurs and Grille du Coq fountains (kit routine hittorffFountain). Basin radius 3.0 m from OSM way 1136105125 (claimed); wall, octagonal pedestal, neck, vasque (~3.7 m across), 12 lion-mask lugs and reed tuft are by eye off Commons photos 'Fontaine de Diane Paris 8e 001-003', not surveyed. Desprez's Diane (~1.8 m) is Modly diane-diane.

name: Fontaine de la Grille du Coq
note: Hittorff's fountain of 1840 (Q3076190) facing the Grille du Coq of the Elysee garden, the one sister of Diane/Cirque/Ambassadeurs with no sculpture (kit hittorffFountain with a plain jet). Position and 3.0 m basin radius from OSM way 67092064 (claimed); Wikidata/frwiki coordinates (48.8674, 2.3180) just copy the Ambassadeurs fountain and are wrong. Pedestal, neck, vasque and jet sizes copy the sister fountains, by eye, not surveyed. No Modly piece.

name: Fontaine du Théâtre-Français — Nymphe marine
note: Davioud's twin fountains of 1872-74 in the place André-Malraux (1er), one drawing for both (src/render/landmarks/paris/monuments/minor/fontaine-theatre-francais.ts). Basin width measured from the OSM way (amenity=fountain + water + wall, 11.3 m across); every height, the bowls and the column are by eye off Commons photos (2026-08 set, Fontaine Nymphe Marine / Fluviale Paris 2, 5, 9). Nymphe marine with an oar by Carrier-Belleuse (Q3076333) and four seated putti by Eude: Modly pieces theatre-marine-nymphe, theatre-marine-putti.

name: Fontaine du Théâtre-Français — Nymphe fluviale
note: Davioud's twin fountains of 1872-74 in the place André-Malraux (1er), one drawing for both (src/render/landmarks/paris/monuments/minor/fontaine-theatre-francais.ts). Basin width measured from the OSM way (amenity=fountain + water + wall, 11.3 m across); every height, the bowls and the column are by eye off Commons photos (2026-08 set, Fontaine Nymphe Marine / Fluviale Paris 2, 5, 9). Winged Nymphe fluviale with a reed by Moreau and four seated putti by Gauthier: Modly pieces theatre-fluviale-nymphe, theatre-fluviale-putti.

name: Pyramide du bois de Vincennes
note: Obelisk of 1731 (Q3411287, Slodtz brothers) on the central island of the carrefour de la Pyramide, Wikidata coordinates; no OSM building there. Three round steps, rusticated square pedestal with banded courses, tapering shaft, rocaille cartouche on each face (shallow relief, procedural), ball and gilt spike. No height is written anywhere: ~17 m total, pedestal ~5 m, steps ~11 m across are scaled by eye off Commons Paris - Pyramide du bois de Vincennes - 020. No Modly pieces: only shallow reliefs.

name: Mausolée de Gaspard Monge
note: Mausolée de Gaspard Monge (Q5526576), Père-Lachaise division 18, OSM way 1211895435 (5.5 x 5.7 m, building=service + historic=tomb, claimed; south face has the door). Rubble crypt with ashlar corner piers, a grilled door in a framed surround, a flat terrace behind an X-braced iron railing, and an Egyptian-style open aedicule (jambs, winged disc, cavetto cornice) holding the marble bust of Monge (Modly tombe-monge-buste, paris-statues.json). Dimensions by eye off Commons photos (door grille ~0.95 m wide), not surveyed; OSM bust node at 48.8603096, 2.3936585.

name: Monument funéraire de Dantan (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q3323375, Père-Lachaise division 4, on Wikidata's point (no OSM building within 12 m; the nearest tomb ways are other graves). Dantan family tomb of 1859: grey slab and name plinth, dark red-brown ledge, ochre stele with green mosaic border and four portrait medallions, mourning women at the corners (Modly dantan-pleureuse-g/-d), cornice, frieze, attic with relief, small corner figures (stand-in blocks). Proportions scaled by eye from Commons 'Dantan div. 4 Père-Lachaise (2)' against a ~1.9 m stele width guess; front faces south (-z) as in the photo, bearing not verified.

name: Tombe d'Héloïse et Abélard
note: Monument funéraire d'Héloïse et Abélard (Q3323370), Père-Lachaise division 7: Lenoir's neo-Gothic open chapel of 1817 (OSM way 313811735, a 5.4 x 5.9 m ring that is the iron fence, tagged building=tomb). Pointed arcades on corner piers and colonnettes, steep slate roof with two gables (trefoil window, roundels, saints, pinnacles, gargoyles), tomb chest inside under the two recumbent effigies (procedural blocks: three Modly attempts at the pair failed, one a split chest-and-figures slab, one a trellis2 box, one a head and hand only). Plan from the OSM ring; body ~3.1 x 3.9 m and height ~6 m scaled by eye off Commons photos, not surveyed. Front (gable) faces bearing ~200 deg, a guess.

name: Cénotaphe de Baudelaire
note: Cénotaphe de Charles Baudelaire (Q3010223, José de Charmoy, 1902), Montparnasse cemetery division 27, at the end of the avenue Transversale against the boundary wall. Placed on the OSM memorial=sculpture node (the Wikidata point is ~4 m off); no OSM building way to claim. Procedural: inscribed slab with a sloping mossy top, plinth, plain stele with coping; the poet-and-genie relief and the recumbent wrapped figure are Modly pieces (baudelaire-poete, baudelaire-gisant in paris-statues.json). Sizes (stele ~3.6 m x 1.3 m, slab ~2.0 x 1.6 x 0.6 m) are scaled by eye off Commons photos against the wall's courses, not surveyed. Front faces bearing ~295 deg (toward the avenue end), a reading of the avenue's direction.

name: Fontaine-labyrinthe (place des Fêtes)
note: Marta Pan's fountain-labyrinth (competition 1980, inaugurated 1986/87; Wikidata Q635634): five eccentric concentric granite walls, each broken by a gap on alternating sides, cobbled floor; dry since ~2015 so no water. Radii, wall height (~0.55 m) and gap angles estimated from one Commons photograph against a car, not surveyed; the orientation (rotateDeg 0) and the amphitheatre steps on one side are not modelled. No OSM way to claim (only points nearby). Purely structural, no Modly piece.

name: Fontaine aux lions du Jardin des plantes
note: The wall fountain of the Jardin des plantes' north entrance (Q137838758, 40 rue Geoffroy-Saint-Hilaire): the retaining wall of Rohault de Fleury's 1834 reservoir, a stone wall with a round arch over a brick cul-de-four, a round basin before it and a lion-head spout; the two bronze lions of Jacquemart (1857/1860) stand on its top corners (Modly jdp-lion, placed from paris-statues.json). OSM way 97183056 (building named Fontaine aux Lions, 8.5 m front edge) claimed; origin = middle of its SE front edge (the polygon lies NW of it), front bearing 151. Wall 8.3 m wide, ~3.3 m high with cornice, arch 3.7 m wide, basin 4.6 m across: scaled off Commons photographs (bollards ~1 m), not surveyed.

name: Fontaine des Arts-et-Métiers
note: Davioud's two oblong Jura-stone basins of 1860 in the square Émile-Chautemps facing the Conservatoire (Q3076248; OSM water ways 30612728 north, 30612729 south: 20.4 x 6.6 m ovals, 27.7 m apart, axes at bearing 111 deg, measured). Each has a stone plinth with a round pedestal, cup and vasque with a jet, and two seated bronzes back to back: Agriculture and Travail (Gumery, north), Mercure and Euterpe (Ottin, south), all four Modly models (arts-metiers-*). Plinth, pedestal and wall heights are by eye off Commons photos against the figures (~1 m), not surveyed.

name: Fontaine du square Tolstoï
note: Three nested hexagonal basins (fr.wikipedia: like Russian dolls) in the square Tolstoï, boulevard Suchet, laid out 1934, under Charles Georges Cassou's marble Femme et enfant of 1934 (Wikidata Q3076299). Placed on OSM node 6943355178 (no basin outline in OSM; no building ways under it). Basin radii, rim heights and the pedestal are estimated by eye off two Commons photos against the ~1.9 m figure, not surveyed; the front (statue faces east, into the square away from the boulevard) is read off a photo's background. The figure is a Modly model (statues manifest tolstoi-femme-enfant).

name: Tombes de La Fontaine et de Molière
note: Père-Lachaise division 25: the matching tombs of La Fontaine (Q3323381) and Molière (Q3323385, the Wikidata item the monuments list calls La Fontaine; both items share 48.86111, 2.39489), moved here together in 1817. Two pale-limestone trough sarcophagi on stepped plinths with a tilted plaque on a corbel at one end and a dark bronze panel on the side, behind a low iron rail. No OSM building way. Sizes by eye from Commons photos (Tombe la fontaine.jpg; Paris Père Lachaise La Fontaine et Molière.JPG); side-by-side spacing, orientation (plaque end toward -z) and the fence are guesses, the fox-and-stork relief is not visible in the photos so is not drawn. No Modly pieces: nothing in the round.

name: Monument aux travailleurs municipaux (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q15156042, Père-Lachaise, on Wikidata's point at a bend of the cemetery road; no OSM building way (only tomb/memorial nodes nearby). The City of Paris's memorial to its employees killed on duty (sewermen, street cleaners, gardeners). Form read off Commons Monument aux travailleurs municipaux 06, 10, 12, 14, 19: pale-limestone obelisk with name panels on a pedestal, panelled double door on the base, two piers with medallions, low curved wall behind, and a veiled seated mourner with a palm (Modly piece travailleurs-figure). Dimensions by eye (Wikidata says ~5 m tall), facing direction is a guess.

name: Monument aux défenseurs de Belfort 1870-1871 (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q94997851, Père-Lachaise division 54 (1911, ~4 m per Wikidata); no OSM building way. Grey-stone memorial: front block with plinth (inscription, bronze lion tablet), two arched wings with bronze portrait medallions, tall pedestal with scrolled cornice; Modly woman and officer bust attached (paris-statues belfort-*). Proportions read by eye from Commons 'Père-Lachaise - Division 54 - Monument à la mémoire des défenseurs de Belfort 1870-71 01.jpg' (160 px/m from the 4 m height); depth guessed 0.9 m; facing east towards Chemin de Mont-Louis guessed from the photo's path.

name: Monument aux victimes de Juin (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q15156018, division 6, chemin de Lesseps, on Wikidata's point (no OSM building way there; the nearby OSM points are trees and tombs). The City of Paris's stele for the dead of June 1832. Form read off Commons Division 6 - Monument aux victimes de juin 01 and 02: rock-faced plinth, tall panel with three name columns under three wreath medallions, dedication band, die with a shallow wreath-and-eagle relief over the motto, cornice with low gable; the relief is shallow so no Modly piece. All dimensions (panel ~1.6 m wide, total ~4.6 m) and the facing direction are estimated by eye, not surveyed.

name: Tombe de l'abbé Delille (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q3323390, division 11, avenue Delille. Claims OSM building way 1210797358 (3.66 x 2.98 m, gabled, the tomb's plot). Form from Commons 'Delille div. 11 Père-Lachaise' and Guyot's drawing: a plain stone tomb house with cornice, low gable and blank front panel in a railed plot on a low kerb. Sizes (tomb 2.4 x 1.4 m, ~1.9 m high) by eye; front faces the avenue (bearing ~63, a guess). No sculpture.

name: Monument funéraire de Legru et Lhenoret (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q3323384, division 1, just north of the cemetery's south entrance (no OSM building way there). Form read off Commons Division 1 - Legru et Lhenoret 01/03 and Tombe Legru-Lhenoret 03: low two-step plinth, a round drum at each end carrying a seated bronze woman (Modly pieces legru-femme-gauche / legru-femme-droite), pale scrolled stele with an oval medallion between them, sloped slab in front, a bronze chain slung between the drums. Sizes (stele ~1.0 m wide, ~1.9 m high, plinth ~3.3 m) and the facing (south, towards the entrance) are estimated by eye, not surveyed.

name: Monument de l'Assistance publique (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q15155995, division 2 section 2, against the cemetery wall on the rue du Repos side, in line with avenue du Bureau; 1911-1930. Form read off Commons Monument Assistance Publique Cimetière Père Lachaise 2024-08-24 and Père-Lachaise - Division 2 - Assistance publique 02, and fr.wikipedia: wide limestone stele, taller pedimented central pillar with a roundel, red inscription Au personnel des hôpitaux de Paris victime du devoir and a black bronze wreath, a 17-name panel each side, palm-relief end pylons, stone-kerbed flower bed in front. Everything shallow or a ring, so no Modly piece. Sizes (pillar ~0.9 m wide, stele ~3.4 m, pillar ~3 m) and the facing (west, away from the wall) are estimated by eye, not surveyed; no OSM building way there.

name: Monument aux victimes non reconnues de l'incendie du Bazar de la Charité
note: Père-Lachaise division 92 (Wikidata Q29650332; 1899, gift of the City of Paris): grey-stone pedestal on two dark granite steps, a round moulded shaft with a leaf collar, an abacus, a die lettered LA VILLE DE PARIS and a small gabled top with the inscription tympanum. OSM has only a node (no building way). Sizes and facing (inscription toward -z) are guesses from two Commons photos; Wikidata width 2 m. Nothing in the round, so no Modly pieces; lettering is blocks, not legible.

name: Jardin mémorial des enfants du Vél' d'Hiv'
note: Memorial garden at 7 rue Nélaton (Q39075133; Mutabilis Paysage, opened 16 July 2017; 120 m2) on the site of the Vélodrome d'Hiver's entrance. Plan from OSM park way 767547602 (no building way under it, nothing to claim) and the wall way 767547603; wall faces north-east. Procedural: gravel court, a concave limestone wall of the deported children's names (about 4,115), a dark steel screen on the street with an entry gap, a trellis with climbers and about twenty photographs, pale stone blocks and grey bands in the gravel. Wall height ~2.3 m, the arc's sagitta (~1.4 m), the screen and block sizes are scaled by eye off Commons photos, not surveyed; names are engraved rows, not legible. Nothing in the round, so no Modly pieces.

name: Monument de la rafle du Vél' d'Hiv' (Spitzer)
note: Walter Spitzer's 1994 monument (architect Mario Azagury; inaugurated 17 July 1994) in the place des Martyrs-Juifs-du-Vélodrome-d'Hiver on the quai de Grenelle, placed on OSM's memorial node (~100 m west of the garden). Procedural: three granite steps, a tapering walkway, an inscribed red-granite pedestal and a concave stone slab (the velodrome's banked curve). Facing south-east toward the quai is a guess; every dimension is scaled by eye off one Commons photo (Monument des Martyrs Juifs du Veledrome d'Hiver.JPG), not surveyed. The bronze group of civilians is Modly vel-dhiv-spitzer-groupe (paris-statues.json).

name: Monument aux morts pour la France en opérations extérieures
note: Q74555507 (inaugurated 11 Nov 2019, Stéphane Vigny), parc André-Citroën. The square plaza is OSM way 672001632 (37 m a side, corners measured, turned to rotateDeg 30). Procedural: slate paving, black granite ring wall (planted top, gilt name rows on the inner face, an entrance gap), flagpole with tricolour. Wall height/thickness, gap and flag position are by eye off Commons photos (Djiril5c 2022 -1, -3; Monument OPEX - Paris 15e). The six bronze soldiers are the Modly piece opex-soldats (paris-statues.json).

name: Pavillon de la Réunion (Jardin d'agronomie tropicale)
note: Q3373069: the 1900 Trocadéro 'kiosque de la Réunion', re-erected in the garden for 1907 and abandoned since (fr.wikipedia, Jardin d'agronomie tropicale). A small dark-timber two-stage pavilion: glazed ground storey, skirt roof, narrower upper stage, shingled hip roof. Footprint is OSM way 62819542 (about 5x4 m); stage heights, window rhythm and colours are by eye off Commons 'Jardin tropical - Paris - Pavillon de la Réunion - 03'; the front bearing is a guess.

name: Monument à la Gloire de l'expansion coloniale française (fragments)
note: Q20055095, Belloc 1913-22. Dismantled in 1961; today five weathered stone pieces lie on the gravel in an arc near the garden entrance (fr.wikipedia; Commons 'Fragments Monument Gloire Expansion Coloniale ...' 2021 and 2026 series). Positions are the five OSM artwork nodes (9592931081-84, 9592962449). Procedural: the low broken-socle slabs; the stone pieces are the Modly models coloniale-republique, -coq, -femme, -couchee (the fifth piece is not modelled). Slab sizes and the pieces' facing are guesses.

name: Monument à la mission Marchand
note: Q3323421, Léon Baudry (1934; fr.wikipedia: a stone wall ~10 m long with a high-relief frieze of the Congo-Nile column, 6 French soldiers and 6 tirailleurs in profile, a route map behind, and a bronze shield naming Marchand and his officers at the right end; on avenue Daumesnil facing the Palais de la Porte Dorée). Claims OSM memorial way 62819232 (12.47 x 1.94 m, long axis bearing 299 deg). Procedural: two steps, wall, cornice, map panel, shield and inscription; the frieze is blocky stand-in figures (the only Commons photo, Monument_Mission_Marchand_Paris_1.jpg, shows just the shield end, so nothing to give Modly). Heights and wall thickness scaled by eye off that photo; the front facing NNE (rotateDeg 151) is inferred from the palace opposite.

name: Monument aux soldats morts pendant le siège de Paris 1870-1871 (Père-Lachaise)
note: Q94696967, Père-Lachaise division 72 (Wikidata label is the Buzenval national-guards memorial, 1877). Form read off Commons Père-Lachaise - Division 72 - Siège de Paris 02, Bataille de Buzenval 01 and the Buzenval 2020 photo: grey-limestone pylon with dentil cornice, hipped cap, wreath roundel, dedication and carved palm; low wing walls with garland-and-rosette frieze; iron railing across the front. All relief is shallow, so no Modly piece. Dimensions by eye against the ~1.1 m railing, not surveyed; facing direction is a guess. No OSM building way.

name: Mémorial des victimes des catastrophes aériennes (Père-Lachaise, div. 77)
note: Q96099792 (labelled the Charm el-Cheikh crash memorial; Wikidata/OSM call the stele Vol 708 West Caribbean, Q2320123), Père-Lachaise division 77, avenue circulaire; placed on the OSM memorial node. Form off Commons Père-Lachaise - Division 72/77 - Vol 708 West Caribbean 01/02: round grey granite disc, black polished centre slab (map of Martinique, title, list of crashes) between two taller grey slabs of names angled inward, small stump at left, dark plaque let into the disc. All procedural, no sculpture. Dimensions by eye (disc ~2.5 m across), not surveyed; facing direction is a guess. No OSM building way to claim.

name: Fontaine Saussure (square Paul-Paray)
note: OSM way 1255942976 (amenity=fountain, name Fontaine Saussure, no Wikidata id): wide shallow pale-tile pool in the square Paul-Paray between rue de Saussure and rue des Tapisseries, 17e. Outline is OSM's; the form (straight tiled back wall, central stone ring, pale blocks, copper-brown lumps) is read off ONE Commons photo (Fontaine Rue Tapisseries 2021-08-21 1). Which side the wall is on, and all heights, are guesses. Ring is procedural (a plain hoop), no Modly piece. The game-supplied point (z 3125) is ~19 m north of the real fountain.
